newsitem.title: ITALY: ITALY MAIN OPPOSITION TO VOTE AGAINST ALBANIA FORCE.
newsitem.headline: ITALY MAIN OPPOSITION TO VOTE AGAINST ALBANIA FORCE.

text.p: Italy's main centre-right opposition Freedom Alliance said it would vote against the government in parliamentary ballots on Tuesday and Wednesday on the deployment of an Italian-led multinational force to Albania.

The announcement by bloc leader Silvio Berlusconi raised a serious threat that Prime Minister Romano Prodi could lose on the government's own motion, a result that would put strong pressure on him to resign.

Berlusconi told reporters after a meeting of opposition leaders that his alliance backed deployment of the force but would vote only for its own motion in the Senate (upper house) later on Tuesday and the Chamber of Deputies on Wednesday.
"We will vote 'no' to the Olive Tree motion on Albania," Berlusconi said, adding he did not see why government parties could not vote for the Freedom Alliance resolution.

Prodi's governing Olive Tree coalition has a majority in the Senate, where it can win, but not in the lower Chamber, where it depends on the hard left Communist Refoundation party for a majority. Refoundation says it will vote 'no' in both houses.

Berlusconi said his alliance had altered its stance of critical support for Prodi after deputy foreign minister Piero Fassino said that the government believed Albanian President Sali Berisha should leave office.
